summary: Cook County, MN: a ladder lookout with lattice legs on Hat Point near Grand Portage; listed as gone, but its stone base remains near the summit trail.

facts.design: Ladder tower with unusual lattice-style legs; also called the Grand Portage lookout
facts.status_note: FFLA lists it as gone; two hiking accounts describe a stone base and metal parts at the summit

access.note: Hiking trail from County Road 17 to the former tower site; Superior Hiking places the mountain within the Grand Portage Reservation; no closure or permit found in the sources read

visit.drive_up: Small parking area on the north side of County Road 17, about 2.4 km east of the village of Grand Portage, marked by a small sign
visit.trail_note: About 400 m along a two-track road, then a trail into the woods climbs about 200 m to the former tower site; one visitor says the trailheads are unmarked and the only sign on the route is about half a mile in

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Forest Fire Lookout Association lists the tower as gone, while two hiking accounts describe a stone base and metal parts at the summit. Both can hold: the tower structure is gone, and part of its base remains.

notes_for_editor: No build or removal date appears in any source read; the A-Z list leaves the year blank, so the story gives design only. No staffing or fire history found. Access is marked public because guides describe the hike; land status comes from one guide, not a tribal or federal record. A Superior Hiking reader asks whether a tree at the end of Hat Point is still there or off limits; that is a question about a different spot, not a stated rule, so not used. The Minnesota Monthly 'abandoned fire tower north of Grand Portage' and the Facebook Presque Isle tower do not name Mount Josephine, so not used. AllTrails returned 403 when fetched.
